title: GIT_DELETED_SET garbage-overcount escapes PROP-103's lower-bound-only trust gate — add upper-bound/ratio sanity + post-sync resurrection assertion to kill the surviving prune<->workspace-sync re-add loop
executive_summary: The prune<->workspace-sync resurrection loop is STILL LIVE despite PROP-094 (depth-independent GIT_DELETED_SET from archive ledger) and PROP-103 (fail-closed when set is empty). The PROP-099 canary fired this run at 312 resurrected integrity artifacts in 48h (107 narrative-cite-audit + 205 verify-pending-run), all present in git HEAD after prune-integrity tombstoned them. PROP-103's own verification_pattern step 5 ('residue drops to 0 and stays 0') is therefore failing. Root cause: GIT_DELETED_SET build is unstable — observed counts include 0 and 70375 (vs ~20631 real archive lines). The 70375-count build on run-2026-06-20T09-13-21Z (the workspace-sync run immediately after the 06-20 08:06 prune) re-added 18 narrative-cite-audit files. PROP-103's trust gate only checks the LOWER bound (count<50 && archives>=50 => untrusted); a garbage OVERCOUNT (count >> archive_lines) sails through with untrusted=false, so grep -qFx fails to match the real tombstoned paths and they flood back as cp re-adds.
evidence: PROP-099 canary RC=3 this run: {narrative-cite-audit-archive.jsonl:107, verify-pending-runs-archive.jsonl:205}, total 312, window 48h.

git log monitor/integrity/narrative-cite-audit-2026-06-19T2309Z.json: deleted at b24f419 (prune-integrity 2026-06-21 08:06) then re-added at 3e1924e (Workspace sync 2026-06-21 09:13). Recurs each prune+sync cycle (also 06-21 11:11/21:08/23:24).

That path IS in a freshly-rebuilt GIT_DELETED_SET (count 2510) and its pre-delete blob sha1 (d973c58...) == current HEAD blob — so the producer-recreation exception (smart_copy lines 600-617) is NOT the escape route; these are immutable per-run artifacts, not regenerated.

workspace-sync run reports show git_deleted_count flapping: distribution incl. {0:3 runs, 70375:1 run} all with git_deleted_set_untrusted=false. run-2026-06-20T09-13-21Z had count=70375 and agent_notes '18 new narrative-cite-audit files' — the resurrection event.

PROP-103 trust gate (workspace-sync.md ~line 763): `if [ ARCHIVE_LINES >= 50 ] && [ GIT_DELETED_COUNT < 50 ]` => only the lower bound; no upper-bound or ratio check. A 70375 overcount is never flagged untrusted.

Net effect: 100 narrative-cite-audit-*.json + 365 verify-pending-run*.json in HEAD that prune wants gone; monitor/integrity working tree ~170MB. Defeats prune-integrity's retention purpose and slowly erodes clone disk headroom (the recurring disk-pressure failure class).
root_cause: PROP-103 made the trust gate fail-closed on an EMPTY/undersized set but assumed a built set is trustworthy. It is not: the archive-ledger->set build can also OVER-produce (count 70375 >> ~20631 archive lines), almost certainly from malformed/multi-line archive records (verify-pending-runs-archive.jsonl carries a `body` field whose embedded JSON can contain newlines that the line-split mis-parses, and/or path-format mismatches) yielding a set of garbage strings that grep -qFx cannot match against real repo-relative paths. With no upper-bound/ratio sanity and no post-sync assertion that no just-tombstoned path was re-added, the garbage-set cycle silently re-adds everything prune deleted.

proposed_fix.philosophy: Extend PROP-103's trust gate from lower-bound-only to a two-sided sanity band, and add a cheap post-sync assertion so a bad cycle fails loud instead of silently resurrecting. Do NOT hand-edit retention math; keep changes inside the existing GIT_DELETED_SET trust block + a new end-of-sync check.
proposed_fix.fix_A_two_sided_trust_gate: In workspace-sync.md after GIT_DELETED_COUNT/ARCHIVE_LINES are computed, set GIT_DELETED_SET_UNTRUSTED=1 ALSO when the set is implausibly large relative to the archive ledger: e.g. `GIT_DELETED_COUNT > ARCHIVE_LINES` (a sort -u set can never legitimately exceed the number of archive records) OR `GIT_DELETED_COUNT > 1.5*ARCHIVE_LINES`. Reuse the existing fail-closed SKIP path (prune-managed integrity categories are skipped, non-prune paths unaffected) and write the same untrusted sentinel. This closes the 70375 case.
proposed_fix.fix_B_robust_set_build: Harden the archive->set extraction so a `body` field containing embedded newlines cannot inflate/corrupt the path list: parse each archive with a streaming JSON-per-line reader that tolerates and skips malformed fragments, and after extraction validate each emitted path with a regex (`^monitor/integrity/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+)*$`) before sort -u. Drop non-matching lines. This prevents garbage strings from ever entering the set.
proposed_fix.fix_C_post_sync_resurrection_assertion: At end of each workspace-sync run, before reporting success, run `node monitor/scripts/check-prune-resurrection.js --hours 2` (narrow window = just-this-cycle). If RC=3, write monitor/integrity/workspace-sync-resurrection-abort-<ts>.json and surface a loud agent_note (NOT silent success). This makes a bad cycle self-evident on the very run that caused it, rather than waiting for the daily tinker canary.

rejected_alternatives: Hand-deleting the 312 resurrected files now without fixing the build: they re-appear next prune+sync cycle (this is exactly what happened after the operator's 06-13 manual drain of 308 files).
Disabling workspace-sync's rescue of monitor/integrity entirely: would break the legitimate universal-pusher rescue of genuinely-new integrity artifacts that haven't been pushed by their producer.
Tightening prune retention to delete fewer files: orthogonal — the bug is re-add, not over-prune.
backfill_plan: After fix lands and one prune+sync cycle completes, the 312 residue should drop to 0 via the next prune (which re-tombstones+deletes them) followed by a now-suppressing workspace-sync. If residue persists >1 cycle, the operator can one-shot delete via the Git Data API tree-delete path (CLAUDE.md escape hatch) since FUSE can't unlink.
verification_pattern: Grade A. Run `node monitor/scripts/check-prune-resurrection.js --hours 48`; exit code 0 (clean) => FIXED. Currently exits 3 with 312 resurrected. After fix + one prune+sync cycle, expect RC=0 sustained across 2 consecutive daily tinker runs. Secondary: grep workspace-sync run reports for any `git_deleted_count` > `archive_lines` with `git_deleted_set_untrusted:false` => should be empty.
constraints_honored: workspace-sync.md changes are operator-review-gated given the 2026-05-21 mass-delete history.
cross_references: PROP-103 (lower-bound fail-closed gate this PROP extends)

Q2_fix_A_diff.title: Fix A — two-sided trust gate (upper bound)
Q2_fix_A_diff.threshold_decision: Use STRICT `GIT_DELETED_COUNT > ARCHIVE_LINES` (NOT 1.5x). Justification: the set is `sort -u` over exactly one .file path per archive record, so unique_paths <= records is a hard mathematical invariant; ANY excess is corruption by construction. The 1.5x band PROP-113 floated needlessly tolerates 1.0x-1.5x corruption with no upside. Smoke test T4 confirms the invariant holds on well-formed input. Guard with `ARCHIVE_LINES >= 50` (mirrors PROP-103 low-side guard) so a near-empty fresh archive cannot trip it, and `GIT_DELETED_SET_UNTRUSTED -eq 0` so it does not double-fire after the low-side gate.
Q2_fix_A_diff.self_contained: Yes — Fix A alone (without B or C) closes the observed 70375 case. It needs no other change; the smart_copy SKIP consumer at lines 628-643 already honors the flag.
Q2_fix_A_diff.validated: old_string matches workspace-sync.md exactly once at commit aecf923.
Q2_fix_A_diff.old_string:
printf '{"ts":"%s","reason":"PROP-103 GIT_DELETED_SET trust gate","git_deleted_count":%d,"archive_lines":%d,"action":"skip prune-managed integrity rescues this cycle"}\n' \
    "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "$GIT_DELETED_COUNT" "$ARCHIVE_LINES" > "$SENTINEL" 2>/dev/null || true
fi
export GIT_DELETED_SET_UNTRUSTED GIT_DELETED_COUNT ARCHIVE_LINES
Q2_fix_A_diff.new_string:
printf '{"ts":"%s","reason":"PROP-103 GIT_DELETED_SET trust gate","git_deleted_count":%d,"archive_lines":%d,"action":"skip prune-managed integrity rescues this cycle"}\n' \
    "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "$GIT_DELETED_COUNT" "$ARCHIVE_LINES" > "$SENTINEL" 2>/dev/null || true
fi
# PROP-113 Fix A (2026-06-22): two-sided trust gate — UPPER bound.
# PROP-103 only fail-closes on an undersized set (count<50 while archives>=50).
# A garbage OVERCOUNT sails through: the 2026-06-20T09:13Z run built
# GIT_DELETED_COUNT=70375 against ARCHIVE_LINES=20631 (3.41x), all paths garbage,
# so grep -qFx matched none of the real tombstones and 18 narrative-cite files
# flooded back. The set is built by `sort -u` over one-.file-path-per-record
# extractions, so the unique-path count can NEVER legitimately exceed the number
# of archive records: GIT_DELETED_COUNT > ARCHIVE_LINES is, by construction, a
# corruption signal. Fail-closed on it exactly as PROP-103 does on the low side.
if [ "$GIT_DELETED_SET_UNTRUSTED" -eq 0 ] && [ "$ARCHIVE_LINES" -ge 50 ] && [ "$GIT_DELETED_COUNT" -gt "$ARCHIVE_LINES" ]; then
  GIT_DELETED_SET_UNTRUSTED=1
  echo "[PROP-113] FAIL-CLOSED (upper bound): GIT_DELETED_COUNT=${GIT_DELETED_COUNT} > archive_lines=${ARCHIVE_LINES} — set build over-produced (garbage); prune-managed integrity rescues will be SKIPPED this cycle"
  SENTINEL_OVER="monitor/integrity/workspace-sync-deleted-set-untrusted-$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H-%M-%SZ).json"
  printf '{"ts":"%s","reason":"PROP-113 GIT_DELETED_SET upper-bound trust gate","git_deleted_count":%d,"archive_lines":%d,"action":"skip prune-managed integrity rescues this cycle"}\n' \
    "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "$GIT_DELETED_COUNT" "$ARCHIVE_LINES" > "$SENTINEL_OVER" 2>/dev/null || true
fi
export GIT_DELETED_SET_UNTRUSTED GIT_DELETED_COUNT ARCHIVE_LINES

Q3_fix_B.title: Fix B — robust set build via hardened helper (PROP-066 extraction pattern)
Q3_fix_B.regex_decision: WIDENED from PROP-113-as-written `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` to `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]` (added colon). Justification: real tombstoned filenames use ISO timestamps that sometimes carry colons (e.g. push-failure-2026-05-06T13:21:02Z.json, run-2026-06-04T03:10:14Z.json). The PROP-113 regex drops these 3 legitimate paths -> workspace-sync would then NOT skip them and could RESURRECT them: a regression worse than the bug. Char inventory across all current archives is exactly [-.0-9:TZ a-z]; colon is the only addition required. ADDED a separate `..`-segment guard (smoke test T2 caught that `..` passes the char-class because dots are legal) to block path traversal.

diff.old_string:
GIT_DELETED_SET="/tmp/git-deleted-set-$$-${RANDOM}.txt"
: > "$GIT_DELETED_SET"
for archive in monitor/integrity/*-archive.jsonl; do
  [ -f "$archive" ] || continue
  # Extract the .file field from each tombstone record (jq if available,
  # node fallback). Output one path per line. Prepend "monitor/integrity/"
  # to bare basenames since smart_copy passes full repo-relative paths.
  if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    jq -r 'select(.file != null) | .file' "$archive" 2>/dev/null
  else
    node -e "
      const fs=require('fs');
      const lines=fs.readFileSync('$archive','utf8').split(String.fromCharCode(10));
      for(const l of lines){if(!l.trim())continue;try{const r=JSON.parse(l);if(r.file)console.log(r.file);}catch(e){}}
    " 2>/dev/null
  fi
done | awk '{ if($0 ~ /\//) print $0; else print "monitor/integrity/" $0 }' | sort -u > "$GIT_DELETED_SET"
GIT_DELETED_COUNT=$(wc -l < "$GIT_DELETED_SET" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
diff.new_string:
GIT_DELETED_SET="/tmp/git-deleted-set-$$-${RANDOM}.txt"
# PROP-113 Fix B (2026-06-22): build the set via a hardened helper instead of the
# inline jq/node|awk|sort pipeline. The helper parses each archive line as JSON,
# rejects any .file containing a newline or failing the integrity-path regex
# (^monitor/integrity/[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+(/...)*$), then writes sorted-unique paths.
# This stops malformed/multi-line archive records from emitting path fragments
# that inflate the set (root cause of the 70375 overcount). The helper ALWAYS
# exits 0 and degrades to an empty set on error, so the PROP-103 lower-bound gate
# still fail-closes. Its stderr is a one-line JSON summary
# {records_seen,parse_failures,paths_emitted,rejected} — a rising `rejected` is the
# early warning for intermittent archive corruption. Extraction-pattern precedent:
# sync-workspace-step4c.js (PROP-066).
GDS_SUMMARY=$(node monitor/scripts/build-git-deleted-set.js --integrity-dir monitor/integrity --out "$GIT_DELETED_SET" 2>&1 >/dev/null) || : > "$GIT_DELETED_SET"
echo "[PROP-113 Fix B] git-deleted-set build: ${GDS_SUMMARY}"
GIT_DELETED_COUNT=$(wc -l < "$GIT_DELETED_SET" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)

validation.clean_parity: Helper emits exactly 2510 paths against the live archives (20631 records), 0 rejected — byte-identical set to the old jq/awk pipeline (comm -3 empty both directions).
validation.garbage_rejection: Injected newline-fragment, absolute-path, and `..`-traversal records are all dropped; 0 leaked into the set.
validation.degrade_safe: Helper always exits 0 and writes an empty set on any error, so the PROP-103 + Fix A lower/upper gates still fail-closed if the build itself fails.
validation.observability: Helper stderr is one-line JSON {records_seen,parse_failures,paths_emitted,rejected}; the diff captures it into GDS_SUMMARY and echoes it. A rising `rejected` is the early-warning canary for intermittent archive corruption.

Q4_fix_C.title: Fix C — post-sync resurrection assertion
Q4_fix_C.window_decision: Use `--hours 2`. Justification: prune+sync cadence is well under 2h (workspace-sync every 2h per PROP-110, prune daily 09:00), so a 2h window captures exactly this-cycle resurrections without re-flagging the pre-existing 312-artifact residue (which a 48h window would, aborting every run until backfill drains). `--hours 1` risks missing a resurrection if the sync runs >1h after the prune; 2h is the safe narrow window.
Q4_fix_C.sentinel_format: monitor/integrity/workspace-sync-resurrection-abort-<ts>.json, mirroring the PROP-051 workspace-sync-abort-*.json shape: {event, timestamp, gate, window_hours, resurrected_total, by_category, reason, operator_action, agent}. Retention: add to the prune-integrity 30-day class alongside workspace-sync-abort-*.json (line ~511).
Q4_fix_C.non_fatal: The data commit (4a) already pushed before this check; Fix C does NOT roll it back (the rescue already happened). It makes the bad cycle self-evident the same run via a loud sentinel + report field, rather than waiting for the daily tinker canary.

part1_assertion_block.old_string: # --- Capture FILES_COMMITTED NOW, AFTER 4a so it reads the workspace-sync commit ---
part1_assertion_block.new_string:
# --- PROP-113 Fix C (2026-06-22): post-sync resurrection assertion ---
# Before finalizing this run's report, assert this cycle did NOT re-add any path
# prune-integrity tombstoned. --hours 2 narrows to just-this-cycle (prune+sync
# cadence is well under 2h; a wider window re-flags pre-existing residue and would
# abort every run until backfill drains). RC=3 => a resurrection happened THIS
# cycle: write a loud abort sentinel so integrity/tinker see it the same day instead
# of inferring it from prose. Non-fatal to the already-pushed data commit — the
# rescue already happened; this makes a bad cycle self-evident on the run that caused it.
RESURRECTION_STATUS="clean"
if [ -f monitor/scripts/check-prune-resurrection.js ]; then
  RESURRECTION_OUT=$(node monitor/scripts/check-prune-resurrection.js --hours 2 2>/dev/null)
  RESURRECTION_RC=$?
  if [ "$RESURRECTION_RC" -eq 3 ]; then
    RESURRECTION_STATUS="ABORT-resurrection-detected"
    RES_SENTINEL="monitor/integrity/workspace-sync-resurrection-abort-$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H-%M-%SZ).json"
    RES_SENTINEL="$RES_SENTINEL" RES_OUT="$RESURRECTION_OUT" node -e '
      const fs=require("fs");
      let detail={}; try{detail=JSON.parse(process.env.RES_OUT||"{}");}catch(e){}
      fs.writeFileSync(process.env.RES_SENTINEL, JSON.stringify({
        event:"workspace-sync-resurrection-abort",
        timestamp:new Date().toISOString(),
        gate:"PROP-113 Fix C post-sync resurrection assertion",
        window_hours:2,
        resurrected_total: detail.resurrected_total!=null?detail.resurrected_total:null,
        by_category: detail.by_category||null,
        reason:"workspace-sync re-added prune-tombstoned integrity artifact(s) this cycle; GIT_DELETED_SET likely untrusted/overcount. See PROP-113.",
        operator_action:"Inspect this run report + any deleted-set-untrusted sentinel; verify PROP-113 Fix A/B gate fired. Next prune cycle should re-tombstone; if residue persists, Git Data API tree-delete (CLAUDE.md escape hatch).",
        agent:"workspace-sync"
      }, null, 2));
    ' 2>/dev/null || true
    git add "$RES_SENTINEL" 2>/dev/null
    echo "[PROP-113 Fix C] WARNING resurrection detected this cycle — wrote $RES_SENTINEL"
  fi
fi

# --- Capture FILES_COMMITTED NOW, AFTER 4a so it reads the workspace-sync commit ---

part2b_report_field.new_string:
archive_lines: parseInt(process.env.ARCHIVE_LINES||'0',10),
  // PROP-113 Fix C: post-sync resurrection assertion result (clean | ABORT-resurrection-detected).
  resurrection_status: process.env.RESURRECTION_STATUS || 'clean',
  agent_notes: process.env.AGENT_NOTES || '',

Q4_fix_C.note: Part 1 is the load-bearing assertion + sentinel. Parts 2a/2b add resurrection_status to the run report (recommended for tinker/integrity grep but optional — Part 1 stands alone). All three old_strings match workspace-sync.md exactly once at commit aecf923.

fix_A.worst_case: Stricter gate fires when it should not, hard-skipping prune-managed integrity rescues indefinitely. But this can only happen if GIT_DELETED_COUNT genuinely exceeds ARCHIVE_LINES, which is impossible on well-formed input (invariant). The realistic false-positive is a transient mid-write read of an archive being appended — one cycle of skipped rescues, self-heals next cycle.
fix_A.blast_radius: Bounded and benign: skipping a prune-managed rescue for one cycle leaves files prune ALREADY wanted gone out of the tree. It cannot delete anything (it only suppresses a cp re-add). This is the OPPOSITE failure direction from the 2026-05-21 mass-delete.
fix_A.detect: Every trip writes workspace-sync-deleted-set-untrusted-*.json with reason "PROP-113 GIT_DELETED_SET upper-bound trust gate". Integrity (daily 02:00) + tinker Mode 2 grep these. If the sentinel appears every cycle, the build is chronically corrupt -> escalate to Fix B.
fix_A.rollback: Operator reverts the Fix A block in workspace-sync.md (git-owned; edit in /tmp/edit-clone, build.js publish). No scheduled-task pause needed — reverting restores PROP-103-only behavior, which is the current production state. Sentinel proving rollback: absence of new upper-bound sentinels after the revert commit.

fix_B.worst_case: Helper mis-classifies a legitimate archive line as malformed and drops a real tombstoned path -> that path is no longer in the set -> workspace-sync resurrects it. This is the regression the colon-regex widening + parity test specifically guard against.
fix_B.blast_radius: A dropped path = one resurrected artifact per cycle (bloat, not data loss). NOT a mass-delete vector — the helper only builds a skip-set; it never deletes.
fix_B.detect: (1) Helper stderr `rejected` count in GDS_SUMMARY — a jump from the expected ~0 is the signal. (2) Fix C resurrection assertion fires within the same cycle if a dropped path actually re-appears. (3) test-prop-113.js parity test (run pre-ship and in any later regression check) catches a builder that diverges from the naive pipeline on clean data.
fix_B.rollback: Revert the Fix B diff (restores the inline pipeline) AND remove monitor/scripts/build-git-deleted-set.js. Since the helper is new, reverting the workspace-sync.md block is sufficient to stop calling it; the orphaned script is inert. Sentinel proving rollback: GDS_SUMMARY echo line disappears from run logs (the inline pipeline does not emit it).

fix_C.worst_case: check-prune-resurrection.js has its own bug and returns RC=3 spuriously -> Fix C writes a false abort sentinel every run. Note: Fix C is assertion-only; a false positive does NOT block the data commit (already pushed) and does NOT delete anything. Worst case is sentinel noise + a false resurrection_status in the report.
fix_C.blast_radius: Cosmetic/observability only. No deletion, no skipped rescue, no commit change. Strictly safer than A or B.
fix_C.detect: A flood of workspace-sync-resurrection-abort-*.json with resurrected_total that does not match independent canary runs. Tinker cross-checks against its own daily --hours 48 canary.
fix_C.rollback: Revert the Fix C diffs. check-prune-resurrection.js is unchanged by this PROP (read-only, PROP-099), so no script rollback needed. Sentinel proving rollback: no new resurrection-abort sentinels after the revert commit.
